label: initiation or admission into a circle
description: Circle language denotes entry into an initiated religious group and receipt of esoteric learning in a quoted Gardner claim.
notes: Not a universal circle meaning and not geometric evidence.

label: female component of deity
description: The source attributes this symbolic meaning to Isis within an occultist interpretive framework.
notes: Meaning remains tied to this source's framework.

label: unconscious or repressed sexuality
description: The source groups Pan, the Horned God, Set, and Satan under this symbolic interpretation.
notes: One grouped prose assertion; not four independent meaning witnesses.

label: balance between conscious and unconscious forces
description: The source says White and Black Pillars represent this balance in Freemasonry and High Magick.
tradition: Freemasonry and High Magick as summarized by the author
notes: No pillar figure is shown in this source.

label: document authentication or witnessing
description: The referenced signature and seal authenticate or witness an OTO charter document.
notes: Excluded from operative magical-geometry correlations.

label: poison protection and treachery detection
description: Norse stories in the source attribute protective and warning functions to runes carved into drinking cups.
tradition: Norse legend as reported in a modern witchcraft beverage manual
notes: No rune forms are shown; the attribution remains tied to the source's retelling.

label: Goddess alignment through womb-like vessel shape
description: The source associates cups with the Goddess because of their womb-like shape.
notes: No vessel drawing is shown.

label: God alignment through squared vessel shape
description: The source recommends squared-off drinking vessels for stronger alignment with the God aspect.
notes: The source does not link squared vessels to Earth in this passage.

label: balance and symmetry through complementary form
description: The source recommends equal ingredient measures and optionally a yin/yang-styled cup to reinforce balance and symmetry.
notes: No yin-yang vessel image is present.

label: fourfold seasonal elemental directional framework
description: The source maps Spring/Air/East/dawn, Summer/Fire/South/noon, Fall/Water/West/dusk, and Winter/Earth/North/midnight.
notes: The four tuples are one framework and are not independent tradition witnesses.

label: divination creativity and Air through pentagram-like natural form
description: The source uses sliced star fruit in an Air-associated recipe and explicitly likens its natural shape to a pentagram.
notes: No star-fruit image or measured geometry is present.

label: Qabala Baphometa or Kylkhor activation
description: The source assigns the page-31 sigil an activation role within its Qabala Baphometa/Kylkhor instructional system.
notes: The accompanying 72-force statement is textual context, not visible numerology.

label: magical battery representation and charging
description: The source presents the page-38 sigil as the sign of a magical battery used to collect or direct magical force.
notes: Meaning is tied to this author's system.

label: ritual-circle band encoding
description: Compact glyph sequences are assigned to the spaces between double or triple ritual-circle boundaries.
notes: Three raw sequence witnesses share one construction family and one authorial source.

label: materialization focus
description: The source identifies the page-44 figure as a materialization sigil.
notes: No universal meaning is inferred from the embedded pentagram.

label: Golem Mass liturgical identity
description: The source identifies the page-45 figure with the Golem Mass.
notes: Stored as a liturgical identity role rather than a cross-tradition geometry-purpose rule.

label: symbolic contact with a magical egregor
description: The source's symbolic method presents conventional magical symbols as contact interfaces for a magical egregor.
notes: The row is one source-level symbol set, not seven independent meaning witnesses.

label: Baphometum entity evocation
description: The source assigns both a double-circle band sequence and an entity-specific sigil to a Baphometum evocation exercise.
notes: Separates environmental band encoding from the entity-specific identity glyph.

label: Pluto-associated genius evocation
description: The source assigns the page-63 triple-circle sequence to evocation of Pluto-associated genii.
notes: The association is modern and source-scoped, not evidence of an ancient Pluto lineage.

label: Umoluman identity or evocation
description: The source identifies the page-64 figure as the sigil of Umoluman.
notes: Entity identity and evocation role remain source-scoped.

label: Lilith identity or evocation
description: The source identifies the page-70 figure as a Lilith sigil within its ritual system.
notes: No claim is made that this is a historically inherited Lilith seal.

label: Urdämonium identity and materialization
description: The source identifies the repeated-triangle figure with its Urdämonium evocation or materialization work.
notes: A secondary page-77 mark is folded into the same principal group.

label: sigil-programmed device or transmission concept
description: The source presents a technical schematic in which a sigil is inserted into an experimental signal or electrical device.
notes: Only the conceptual topology is retained; hazardous operating specifications are excluded.

label: Sun Moon and eight Sabbats emblem
description: The Seax-Wica emblem is explicitly said to symbolize the Sun, Moon, and eight Sabbats or Wheel of the Year.
notes: Meaning is explicit in the frontispiece caption.

label: Seax-Wica Futhorc writing and ritual reference
description: The source presents Saxon/Anglo-Saxon Futhorc tables as the rune forms favored by Seax-Wica and as writing or ritual references.
tradition: Saxon/Anglo-Saxon runic tradition as presented by modern Seax-Wica
notes: Two visual witnesses share one broad Futhorc lineage.

label: ritual spatial organization of tools and roles
description: The circular altar diagram assigns deity figures, candle, censer, water, salt, sword, book, drinking horn, and officiant roles to defined locations.
notes: Purpose derives from the labeled layout and adjacent instructions.

label: eightfold annual seasonal calendar
description: The Wheel of the Year diagram organizes seasons, solstices/equinoxes, and eight Sabbats around a cycle.
tradition: modern Seax-Wica / modern Pagan seasonal calendar
notes: The eightfold radial structure is visually explicit.

label: sympathetic human proxy construction and personalization
description: The poppet diagram shows how a cloth human proxy is cut, sewn, and marked with identifying or astrological features.
notes: Operational manipulation instructions are not reproduced.

label: directed nine-node card-reading sequence
description: The Path layout assigns a Significator and eight cards to a directed sequence of semantic reading positions.
notes: Nine nodes include the Significator plus eight numbered cards.

label: magical alphabet substitution writing
description: Theban, Passing the River, Malachim, and Celestial tables provide named substitution scripts for esoteric writing.
tradition: magical alphabets reproduced in a modern Seax-Wica manual
notes: Four distinct named lineages share one table-representation grammar.

label: Ogham inscription reference
description: The Ogham plate presents a stemline-based script described as useful for carving inscriptions on stone or wood.
tradition: Ogham as reproduced in a modern Seax-Wica manual
notes: Historical description is secondary-source context.

label: Germanic rune writing divination and ritual reference
description: The Germanic rune table is presented within a discussion of runes as writing systems used for divinatory and ritual purposes.
tradition: Germanic runic tradition as reproduced in a modern Seax-Wica manual
notes: One modern reference witness; no independent artifact provenance.

label: Scandinavian rune variant reference
description: The Scandinavian plate compares Danish and Swedish-Norse rune variants with phonetic values.
tradition: Danish and Swedish-Norse rune traditions as reproduced in a modern Seax-Wica manual
notes: Two subtables are retained within one principal plate.

label: ritual enclosure with replaceable cosmological payload
description: The Circle of Art defines a protected ritual field while its inscription bands and sectors receive operation-specific angelic, seasonal, temporal, lunar, and solar names.
tradition: modern ceremonial magic drawing from the Heptameron
notes: Fixed geometry and replaceable semantic payload are explicitly distinguished by the adjacent commentary.

label: protection and compelled attention or obedience
description: The source identifies the interlaced six-point pentacle as a protective instrument that demands the appearing spirit's attention or obedience.
tradition: modern ceremonial magic drawing from the Heptameron
notes: Meaning remains tied to this ceremonial source and inherited figure lineage.

label: weekday angelic planetary and zodiacal correspondence payload
description: Seven plates encode Sunday through Saturday by replacing the governing angel name or signature, planetary glyph, and related zodiacal, heaven, or angelic signs within one repeated plate structure.
tradition: modern ceremonial magic reproduction of Heptameron day correspondences
notes: Seven raw plates represent one inherited template family with variable semantic payload.

label: house protection through component-overlay symbolism
description: The source assigns six labeled component signs to a centered composite programming symbol for a house-protection entity.
notes: The six legend items are components of one source-level composite, not independent evidence traditions.

label: semantic distillation by deterministic filtering
description: The source reduces a statement through duplicate-letter deletion, Greek-equivalent filtering, Pythagorean mapping, repeated-number deletion, reconversion, and transliteration.
notes: Stored as construction grammar rather than as a universal magical claim.

label: numerological coordinate-path construction
description: The source uses Pythagorean values and a 3×3 Lo Shu grid to convert distilled semantic material into coordinate and marker instructions for a symbol.
notes: The grid and mapping are visually explicit; numerological interpretations remain source-scoped.

label: inspiration and hindrance removal programming symbol
description: The final circular symbol is assigned to an inspiration-focused entity intended to provide inspiration or remove hindrances.
notes: Meaning is linked to the documented construction chain, not inferred from geometry alone.

label: destructive and harassing case-study assignment
description: The D’watcher symbol is assigned a destructive and harassing purpose in the source's case-study appendix.
notes: Operational instructions and activation details are excluded; only source attribution and visible geometry are retained.

label: multi-purpose thirteen-herb cabinet
description: The source frames thirteen selected herbs as a compact cabinet intended to address a broad range of practical, medicinal, culinary, protective, and magical needs.
notes: The count thirteen is preserved as source structure only; no universal numerological meaning is inferred.

label: quarter calling and fifth salute
description: The source prescribes a calling pentacle, salute, and kiss at each quarter, followed by a final salute to the fifth.
notes: No pentacle image, trace order, or fifth-point location is shown.

label: complete ritual-circle lifecycle
description: The source presents the circle as a boundary that is drawn, consecrated, activated at the quarters, used to bind the work, released, banished, and cut or opened.
notes: This is process evidence, not measured circle geometry.

label: cardinal elements with central Spirit
description: The source maps directions to elements, tools, colors, beings, seasons, times, and qualities, while placing Spirit at the center as balance, invocation, and manifestation.
notes: The four quarter tuples and central Spirit tuple are one source framework rather than five independent traditions.

label: fertility motherhood and Earth-Mother attribution
description: The authors interpret prehistoric Venus figurines as embodiments of fertility and motherhood in the form of a great Earth Mother and connect them to modern Wiccan worship.
notes: Interpretation is attributed to this source and does not establish prehistoric Wiccan continuity.

label: horned male nature and animal-world consort attribution
description: The authors interpret the antlered Sorcerer image as a male consort or husband to the Goddess and as representing the human, natural, and animal worlds.
notes: Interpretation is source-scoped and distinct from the visual description of the reproduced artifact.
